scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Yield tokenization takes a yield-bearing asset (a staked asset, a lending receipt, a stablecoin savings token) and splits it into two tokens that mature on a set date: trades at a discount before then. Buy the discount, hold to maturity, and your return is fixed. the underlying earns until maturity, then is worth zero. P.T. + Y.T. = one unit of the underlying. The P.T. price implies a fixed rate; the Y.T. is a bet that realised yield beats it. fixed A.P.Y. = (1 divided by P.T. price)^(365 divided by days) minus 1 P.T. (principal token): redeems 1:1 for the underlying at maturity. It Y.T. (yield token): receives all the variable yield (and often points)
scenes.cap: PT (principal token): redeems 1:1 for the underlying at maturity. It YT (yield token): receives all the variable yield (and often points)

scenes.title: Worked example
items: the calculator → 8.63% fixed APY if held to maturity.
$100,000 buys ~104,167 PT → redeems for ~104,167 of the underlying at maturity.
The YT costs ~0.04 per unit. It only profits if the underlying's realised
scenes.vo: A stablecoin savings token has a P.T. maturing in 180 days, priced at 0.96. yield (plus any points) averages above about 8.6% for the 180 days. Near maturity, small discounts are big rates: P.T. at 0.985 with 60 days left to 9.63% A.P.Y.. Check liquidity before chasing these; exiting early means selling into the pool. the calculator to 8.63% fixed A.P.Y. if held to maturity. $100,000 buys about 104,167 P.T. to redeems for about 104,167 of the underlying at maturity. lines: PT at 0.97, 120 days to maturity. Fixed APY?
scenes.vo: P.T. at 0.97, 120 days to maturity. Fixed A.P.Y.? ... Pause and think. ... The answer: (1/0.97)^(365/120) minus 1 about 9.7%.
scenes.cap: PT at 0.97, 120 days to maturity. Fixed APY? Pause and think. The answer: (1/0.97)^(365/120) − 1 ≈ 9.7%.

lines: Does buying PT remove the underlying's risk?
scenes.sub: Answer: No. It fixes the rate. If the underlying depegs or is exploited, the PT redeems into a damaged asset.
scenes.vo: Does buying P.T. remove the underlying's risk? ... Pause and think. ... The answer: No. It fixes the rate. If the underlying depegs or is exploited, the P.T. redeems into a damaged asset.

lines: What must happen for a YT to profit?
scenes.sub: Answer: Realised variable yield plus points must beat the implied rate priced into the PT.
